coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Venue
record.summary: Venue is a 147-149 unit apartment building at 1155 4th St, managed by Sares Regis Management; DataSF Assessor records and a RentCafe listing both give 2014 as the building's construction-completion year.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is Assessor lot 8711025 (4,417 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints (mblr SF8711025)); 97% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 95% of the lot.

changes.text: The Assessor roll gives 2014 as year built and DBI recorded the permit complete on 2014-10-01; no source read gives a different year.
Venue now uses its Assessor lot lines.

Venue at 1155 4th St is tagged an apartment building in OpenStreetMap, but the city permit describes 'erect new 6 stories of 147 units condo building'. Whether the homes are rentals or owner-occupied is not settled by the sources read.

The note about the nearby Edwin M. Lee Apartments now cites SF YIMBY (118 units, about 123,700 sq ft) in place of an unsourced 124,000 sq ft figure. The aerial photo credits were corrected: the NAIP credit names the Farm Production and Conservation Business Center, and the Commons photo no longer says it was taken from a departing flight. The Joe & The Juice entry now says the tenant's page names only the address, not the Venue building. The RentCafe-based manager and unit-mix statements are marked as not re-confirmed because that page returns 403.

images.caption: Aerial photo of San Francisco's Mission Bay, ballpark, and Caltrain area
images.appeal_note: Oracle Park's diamond and Chase Center's dome (with its own logo) are both clearly identifiable landmarks in one colorful frame -- reads far better at card size than the flatter government orthophoto.

open_questions: The construction year is given as 2014 by the DataSF Assessor roll (year built 2014 from the 2016 roll on) and by RentCafe's listing text, and DBI's permit is recorded complete on 2014-10-01; no source read gives a different year. The Assessor rolls through 2015 show no year built and no units for this lot. Precise month of completion is not sourced.
Developer/architect not confirmed from any source checked as of 2026-09-29.
No opening date found for Joe & The Juice (1155 4th St): checked its own location page for a firm date; Pier & Point's retail listing also has no opening date for it.

The RentCafe listing could not be checked again on 2026-09-29, so the Sares Regis Management attribution, the unit mix and RentCafe's 'Building constructed in 2014' text could not be re-confirmed; the 2014 year is independently supported by the Assessor roll and the DBI permit completed 2014-10-01.

record.notes: The real, notable Edwin M. Lee Apartments (per SF YIMBY, May 2021: 118 units, about 123,700 sq ft, 62 units for formerly unhoused veterans and 56 for families, at 1150 3rd St, one block away) was investigated for this record but its address point sits ~37m (our own measurement) from this footprint's edge -- close enough to be the nearest available DataSF footprint, but not confidently its own separate outline in the building-footprint data checked. Left out rather than guessed; it should be re-checked with a dedicated satellite/plan comparison.
